title: BNCI 2015-012 PASS2D P300 dataset
description: EEG recordings from 10 mostly BCI-naive healthy participants using PASS2D, a nine-class auditory ERP speller. Users attended to two-dimensional auditory stimuli varying in pitch (high/medium/low) and direction (left/middle/right) presented via headphones, and the resulting nine control signals drove a predictive T9-style text entry system. Each session had a calibration phase followed by online spelling of German sentences. Original-study users spelled about 0.8 characters per minute (3.4 bits/min).
methods_description: 63-channel wet Ag/AgCl EEG (Brain Products, EasyCap, nose reference) was recorded at 250 Hz and downsampled to 100 Hz. Each single session lasted 3-4 hours. Calibration consisted of 3 runs of 9 trials, followed by 2 online spelling runs. Classification used shrinkage-regularized linear Fisher discriminant analysis on amplitudes from N200 and P300 intervals. Epochs with peak-to-peak amplitude above 100 μV were rejected during calibration.
